req.title: Include origin IP in echoed metadata
req.statement: The system shall include the client origin (X-Forwarded-For if present, else remote_addr) in the 'origin' field of all echo endpoints.
triggers: include origin ip in echoed metadata

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that all echo endpoints (/get, /post, /put, /patch, /delete) must include the client origin IP in the 'origin' field, preferring X-Forwarded-For if present, else falling back to remote_addr. The key logic is in get_dict() in helpers.py: `origin=request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-For', request.remote_addr)`. Tests must cover: (1) positive - remote_addr used when no X-Forwarded-For header, (2) positive - X-Forwarded-For used when present, (3) negative - absence of origin field would be a failure, (4) boundary - X-Forwarded-For present but empty string vs. absent, (5) decision table covering all five endpoints. Mutation targets: the string literal 'X-Forwarded-For', the fallback to remote_addr, the field name 'origin', and the presence of origin in each endpoint's get_dict call.

tests.name: test_get_origin_uses_remote_addr_when_no_xff
actions: Send GET /get with no X-Forwarded-For header
Check 'origin' field equals the test client remote_addr (127.0.0.1)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-034: origin field must use remote_addr when X-Forwarded-For absent
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_origin_uses_remote_addr_when_no_xff():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'origin' in data
    assert data['origin'] == '127.0.0.1'

test_get_origin_uses_remote_addr_when_no_xff()

tests.name: test_get_origin_uses_xff_when_present
preconditions: X-Forwarded-For header is set to a specific IP
trace: R-HTTPBIN-034: X-Forwarded-For takes precedence over remote_addr
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_origin_uses_xff_when_present():
    r = client.get('/get', headers={'X-Forwarded-For': '203.0.113.42'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'origin' in data
    assert data['origin'] == '203.0.113.42'
    assert data['origin'] != '127.0.0.1'

tests.name: test_xff_empty_string_used_over_remote_addr
preconditions: X-Forwarded-For header is present but set to empty string
actions: Assert origin equals '' (empty string, not remote_addr) because header IS present
expected: origin == '' (empty string, XFF present but empty takes precedence over remote_addr)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-034: BVA boundary - empty XFF header is still 'present'; get() returns '' not None, so remote_addr fallback is NOT used
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_xff_empty_string_used_over_remote_addr():
    r = client.get('/get', headers={'X-Forwarded-For': ''})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'origin' in data
    # When XFF header is present but empty, headers.get returns ''
    # which is falsy but not None, so the fallback to remote_addr depends
    # on dict.get behavior: headers.get('X-Forwarded-For', remote_addr)
    # returns '' (empty string) since key exists
    assert data['origin'] == ''

test_xff_empty_string_used_over_remote_addr()

tests.name: test_all_echo_endpoints_have_origin_key
preconditions: X-Forwarded-For set to a known IP for all requests
actions: Send GET /get, POST /post, PUT /put, PATCH /patch, DELETE /delete each with X-Forwarded-For: 9.9.9.9
trace: R-HTTPBIN-034: decision table covering all five echo endpoints
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_echo_endpoints_have_origin_key():
    xff = '9.9.9.9'
    headers = {'X-Forwarded-For': xff}
    endpoints = [
        ('GET', '/get'),
        ('POST', '/post'),
        ('PUT', '/put'),
        ('PATCH', '/patch'),
        ('DELETE', '/delete'),
    ]
    for method, path in endpoints:
        r = client.open(path, method=method, headers=headers)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"{method} {path} returned {r.status_code}"
        data = r.get_json()
        assert 'origin' in data, f"{method} {path} missing 'origin'"
        assert data['origin'] == xff, f"{method} {path} origin={data['origin']!r}"

test_all_echo_endpoints_have_origin_key()

from httpbin.core import app

def test_origin_field_name_exact_spelling():
    r = client.get('/get')

    assert 'ip' not in data
